items.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: Like they had a Zane Paul, and Don Leight. Zane Paul, he played bass clarinet and tenor and alto.

ctx.x: Your stamp was all over that thing.

Oh, yeah, yeah. I spent a lot of time trying to get the sound. Like they had a Zane Paul, and Don Leight. Zane Paul, he played bass clarinet and tenor and alto. Don Leight trumpet. Eddy Williams trumpet. And Neal Tate piano, Idris Muhammed on drums, and Charlie Brown acoustic guitar and let’s see who else did we have? Oh, Alan Fontaine, he played guitar, electric guitar. So now what I did, I said now I’ve got to voice this stuff to make it sound different from anything. Because the show is different from anything…

well so I came to see what was happening.” So they said, “we don’t know nothing about that.” They said, “it’s been packed every day and night.” He said, “okay,” so he went up in the big office and talked to some of the people, and told them, “the show is closed as of this minute.” So he closed the show out. Man, but four days before he closed it, somebody stole my bass book. All the other books were there, but my bass book was gone. And so I went down to one of the record companies we were doing business with,…
